_comment: EXAMPLE ONLY — do not use as-is. Run `uv run python setup_wizard.py` to generate a real config.json for YOUR Housecall Pro account. The hcp_id and pipeline-stage id values below are fake; real ones are unique per account, so a config copied between accounts matches nothing and every capacity/pipeline tool silently returns empty. Run `hcp_check_setup` in Claude to confirm your config matches your account.

scheduling.notes: productive_hours_per_day is real working capacity. appointment_window_hours is the window you block on the calendar, including the unpaid break. The DIFFERENCE between them (here 0.5h = 30 min) is subtracted from any day of 6h or more when computing actual worked hours. Set these to match how you actually book days.
scheduling.blended_cost_note: Fully-loaded cost per tech-hour: wages, payroll burden, vehicle, insurance, overhead. This drives every margin number, so use YOUR figure — 95.0 is a placeholder.
scheduling._tuning_notes: Optional. full_day_min_hours: shortest day that gets a break deducted. anchor_tolerance_hours: how far started_at may sit from the scheduled start and still be trusted. early_finish_tolerance_hours: how early completed_at may be and still count as a real early finish (finishing early is real signal; finishing 'late' past the tolerance is usually paperwork after leaving site). cluster_gap_days: gap within which two jobs for the same customer+address are treated as one split project. Defaults are fine unless your crews work unusual patterns.

tags._comment: Optional. A job-tag convention the scheduling tools understand. This is one franchise's system — adopt, change, or delete it. Tools degrade gracefully when tags are absent; they just flag jobs as untagged.

known_quirks: Dollar amounts are integers in CENTS — divide by 100 to display.
Line items endpoint returns {object, data, url} — read 'data', not 'line_items'.
Job date filters are scheduled_start_min / scheduled_start_max and REQUIRE a trailing Z on the timestamp.

work_status filter values (unscheduled/scheduled/in_progress/completed/canceled) differ from the display strings the API returns ('needs scheduling', 'in progress', 'complete rated', ...). The filter must be sent as an array.

Job and Estimate schedule objects use scheduled_start/scheduled_end/arrival_window. Appointment and Event objects use start_time/end_time/arrival_window_minutes. Mixing them up renders '?' rather than erroring.
Only started_at/completed_at exist on work_timestamps — there is no per-tech time tracking and no pause data in the public API.
/api/price_book/services returns service_materials and service_labor_rates as empty arrays unless you pass expand[].
Canceled jobs are archived; /jobs/{id}/appointments returns HTTP 400 'Archived job' for them permanently.
Array query params MUST use the [] suffix. expand[]=attachments works; expand=attachments returns HTTP 400, in both scalar and repeated form. Same for work_status[] and price-book expand[].

Several resources are NOT at the path you would guess, and the wrong one returns a 404 HTML page rather than a JSON error: invoice detail is /api/invoices/{id} (not /invoices/{id}, even though the LIST is /invoices); materials, material_categories and price_forms all live under /api/price_book/; job types are at /job_fields/job_types.
There are NO payment or deposit endpoints in the public API. Sending an invoice and recording a payment can only be done inside Housecall Pro.

Estimates cannot be updated: no PUT/PATCH on /estimates/{id} and no PUT/DELETE on options. You can create an option but never rename or remove one. There is also no endpoint for tagging an estimate - tags exist only for jobs.
There are no messaging, conversation or SMS endpoints, so customer chat history cannot be read through the API at all.

Attachments are readable via expand[]=attachments on jobs and estimates, and hang off each estimate OPTION rather than the estimate itself. The returned S3 URLs are pre-signed and expire after about an hour.

Schedule objects carry scheduled_start_local / scheduled_end_local plus an IANA time_zone (added 2026-08-20). Prefer these for display AND for bucketing work into days - the UTC fields put an evening job on the following day.

Estimate options carry approval_status_updated_at (added 2026-08-26). It moves on EVERY approval transition, including approved -> declined, so it is not an 'approved at' date; read it with approval_status.
Fanning out more than ~90 concurrent job sub-requests draws HTTP 429. Never treat a failed fetch as an empty payload — it silently becomes '0 quoted hours'.

job_cost_import._comment: Rules for hcp_import_job_costs, which posts supplier receipts onto jobs as material actuals. Defaults are in the code; anything set here overrides. The tool previews by default and never posts without dry_run=False — worth keeping that habit, because job input materials CANNOT be deleted through the API, only zeroed out.
job_cost_import._tool_threshold_note: At or above this, a tool purchase is treated as overhead rather than one job's cost. Below it, small tools are flagged for you to decide. A $219 rotary hammer charged to a job gets pulled out; a $27 drill bit does not.
job_cost_import._non_job_labels_note: Values in the receipt's job column that mean 'not a job'. Van and shop stock land here. Add your own conventions.
job_cost_import._skip_note: Food, drink and delivery fees are never a job cost. Matched on the supplier's own department/class columns.

supplier_column_aliases._comment: Home Depot, Lowe's and Sherwin-Williams exports are recognised already. Add another supplier by listing its column names here. FIRST match wins, so order matters.
supplier_column_aliases._job_note: PO Number leads deliberately. Sherwin-Williams also has a 'Job Number' (always 1) and a 'Job Name' (always your own company) — both decoys. Home Depot has no PO column and its 'Job Name' really is the job.
supplier_column_aliases._amount_note: Must be the EXTENDED line total, never a unit price. Lowe's has both ('Item Price' unit, 'Total Price' extended). Sherwin-Williams calls its extended total plain 'Price' while still showing a Quantity — 2 x $93.50 is a $93.50 line there, not $187.

job_cost_import._always_general_note: Always van stock, whatever the receipt says — these get restocked and reused. Matched as lowercase substrings of the item description.
job_cost_import._always_job_note: Always a job material, overriding everything else. Add items you have decided once and do not want asked about again.
job_cost_import._ambiguous_note: Blades, drill bits, sandpaper, tape, brushes, buckets and similar are deliberately NOT guessed — the same drill bit is a job material when bought for that job and van stock when bought to restock the truck. They go to a review list. Route them in bulk with supplies='job' or supplies='general' on the import, or move specific ones into the two lists above once you have decided.
job_cost_import._reuse_note: Leftovers that go back on the van (half a can of primer, say) are not tracked. The whole purchase stays on the job it was bought for, which slightly overstates that job and understates the next one that uses the remainder.
_supplier_notes: Home Depot: cp1252 encoded, not UTF-8. Its 'Company Name' header line is YOUR account, not the store.
Sherwin-Williams: puts the order's PO and date on the FIRST line of each invoice only; later lines are blank and are carried down, matched on Invoice Number.
Lowe's: job is the PO Number, and '00' means no job. Snacks and coffee sit under sub category FRONT END AND CONVENIENCE.
Category words are matched as substrings across department/class/subclass together, because each supplier files food in a different column.
job_cost_import._equipment_note: Things you own and keep using. Overhead at ANY price — the tool threshold does not apply, because a $70 floor fan is shop equipment for the same reason a $700 one is. This is about what the item IS, not what it cost.
job_cost_import._matching_note: All keyword lists match WHOLE WORDS, not substrings. That is deliberate: 'brush' as a substring put a floor register 'in Brushed Nickel' into the review pile. Multi-word entries like 'drill bit' still work.
job_cost_import._billing_context_note: The preview shows each job's materials allowance from its line items next to what the import would spend. The allowances are generic ('List of Materials') so they cannot say whether a given blade belongs to a job, but they show whether a job can absorb the spend — and flag jobs billing NO materials, where every dollar posted comes off the margin.
job_cost_import._overhead_ledger_note: Lines the import decides are NOT job costs are appended to overhead_ledger.csv beside the server (override with the HCP_OVERHEAD_LEDGER environment variable). Read it with hcp_overhead_report. It is deliberately NOT a job in Housecall Pro: a dummy job shows up in every job list, drags portfolio margin because it is all cost and no revenue, needs a fake customer, and has to be excluded by hand from every report forever. It is also deliberately not a database — an append-only list of purchases is a CSV. This is for operational analysis; the expense itself belongs in your accounting software, which already receives these card transactions.
job_cost_import._history_note: To build overhead history from receipts whose jobs are already closed, run the import with overhead_only=true. It records the non-job spend and posts nothing to any job, so you get the analysis without altering finished work. The ledger deduplicates on vendor + receipt + item, so overlapping date ranges are safe to re-run.
